canon_requests.old: Renaming requires an alias entry in `data/aliases.json`.
canon_requests.new: Renaming requires an alias entry: the renamed record lists its old IDs in `aliases` (doc 19 §1.2).
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G2: all content lives under content/<doc>/<ns>/ (doc 02 §11.1)

canon_requests.new: | Namespace prefix | Record owners | Rule owners |  (every row split: the owner cell's two-digit record owners in the second column, phrases such as "Echo acquisition in 15", "account economy rules in 15" and "owners per §11.1 and §12 for behavior" in the third)
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G3: owner cells mix record owners and rule owners; doc 19 §1.4 parses them

canon_requests.old: Every piece of content and every enum value has a string **content ID**.
canon_requests.new: Every piece of content and every enum value that other records reference, or that saves and packets carry as `id32`, has a string **content ID**. A closed set used by one field only is a JSON Schema `enum` of bare words (doc 19 G4).
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G4: part slots, KPI units, flag kinds and axis names are field-local bare words

canon_requests.new: Bp content values are `i32`; power-table values and `i64` table multipliers are `i64` Bp and in content stay within `±(2^53 - 1)` (doc 19 `bp`, `bp_i64`).
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G5: Bp width for i64 power tables

canon_requests.old: Larger values, and every `u64` such as a seed or a hash, are written as `"0x"`-prefixed hexadecimal strings, because JSON tooling loses precision above 2^53.
canon_requests.new: Larger values, and every `u64` such as a seed or a hash, are written as `"0x"` followed by exactly 16 upper-case hexadecimal digits, because JSON tooling loses precision above 2^53 and `content_hash` hashes the JSON text.
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G6: one canonical hex spelling

canon_requests.new: Locale tags are not content IDs. A locale record has the ID `nar.locale.<tag>`, the BCP 47 tag lower-cased with `-` written as `_` (for example `nar.locale.en_us`); doc 18 owns the records.
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G7: BCP 47 tags break the ID grammar

canon_requests.new: Every ID the canon replaces is listed as retired in §17.7, including the block category and the Delving skill IDs replaced in canon-1.4.
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G8: retirements outside §17.7 are invisible to gen_namespaces.py

canon_requests.new: - The integer token `-0` is not an integer; content never contains it.
- A JSON object in content never repeats a key.
canon_requests.why: doc 19 G10: serde_json keeps the last value silently
